name: The Patriarch Tree

location.address: Patriarch Grove, Ancient Bristlecone Pine Forest, Inyo National Forest, White Mountains, Mono/Inyo County, California
location.neighbourhood: Patriarch Grove, on the self-guided Timberline Ancients Trail, about 13 miles north of the Schulman Grove visitor center on a maintained dirt road

access: Paid entry ($3/person, $6/car maximum at the Schulman Grove visitor center gate, children under 18 free); reached via a maintained but rough dirt road (a spare tire is recommended) 13 miles north of Schulman Grove to Patriarch Grove at about 11,300 ft elevation, then a short walk on the Timberline Ancients Trail, encountered almost immediately from the trailhead. The forest is generally open mid-May through November, weather permitting.
transport: No public transit; reached by car via White Mountain Road from US-395 near Big Pine, California.
verify_notes: Widely reported (both sources) as the LARGEST bristlecone pine in the world by trunk volume/girth, standing in a stark, mostly bare rocky landscape at high elevation. Both sources agree it is comparatively less gnarled/twisted than many neighbouring ancient bristlecones nearby, an unusual look for the species at this age. No numeric height, girth or age figure was found in either source fetched this pass; this is the species famous for extreme longevity (Methuselah, in the neighbouring Schulman Grove area, is dated at 4,858 years per Wikipedia) but the Patriarch's own age has not been published in the sources checked, so age is left undocumented rather than guessed. Location is grove/trailhead-level (confirmed coordinate is for the Patriarch Grove trailhead area, not an independently verified tree-level pin), so marked approximate.
note_worth_the_visit: Being the largest of its species, in a starkly beautiful high-elevation setting, is itself the reason to visit; treat as a single-tree destination if the place cannot reach the four-tree floor otherwise.
